en.title: Stem and endings
en.summary: A verb has a stem that carries the meaning and endings that carry grammar.

paragraphs: A verb has a stem, which carries the meaning, and it can take endings that carry grammar. The stem of walks, walked and walking is walk. In English the stem is the same as the base form, so it is easy to find. Knowing the stem helps you see how a verb changes.

English verbs have few endings: -s for the third person singular of the present, -ed for the past and the past participle of regular verbs, and -ing for the participle and the continuous forms. All other grammar is carried by helping verbs. Irregular verbs change the stem itself instead of adding -ed.

blocks.html:

vowel changeirregular pastsing, sang

paragraphs: A final e is dropped before -ing: make, making. A single consonant after a short stressed vowel is doubled: stop, stopping, stopped. A final y after a consonant becomes ie before -s and i before -ed: study, studies, studied.
The ending -ed is said three ways. It is /t/ after voiceless sounds (walked), /d/ after voiced sounds (played) and /ɪd/ after t or d (wanted). The spelling is the same in all three.

items: Wrong: **She walk to work.** Right: **She walks to work.**

ro.title: Tema și terminațiile
ro.summary: Verbul are o rădăcină fixă și terminații care se schimbă pentru fiecare persoană.

paragraphs: Un verb este format din două părți principale. Rădăcina sau tema conține înțelesul de bază al cuvântului. Terminația adăugată la sfârșit arată persoana și timpul acțiunii.
Păstrăm tema verbului și adăugăm terminații diferite. Fiecare persoană are propria terminație în limba română. Astfel, terminația ne arată clar cine face acțiunea.
